description:
Redwood Inference is expanding its Private deployment offerings (VPC and on-prem) with a Day-2 operations toolkit focused on backup/restore and disaster recovery (DR). The project’s goal is to ship a supported, documented, and repeatable set of scripts, automation hooks, and runbooks that enable customers (and Redwood Solutions/SRE teams) to: (1) take consistent backups of control-plane and critical configuration state, (2) restore into a new or existing cluster reliably, and (3) execute DR procedures that meet enterprise RPO/RTO targets. Scope includes: backup/restore for Redwood Private control plane state (datastores, configuration, secrets references), cluster-level dependencies (Kubernetes manifests/Helm release values, etcd snapshots where applicable), and operational validation (smoke tests, game days, observability/alerts). It also includes packaging considerations for on-prem/air-gapped installs (signed artifacts, offline docs, deterministic bundle layout) and cloud-specific guidance for VPC deployments (S3/KMS/IAM patterns and restore staging).

Primary stakeholders: Private Deployments Product (Vivek Kulkarni) for requirements and customer expectations; Platform/Control Plane Engineering (Priya Natarajan, Ethan Park) for any product surfaces and APIs needed; Infrastructure & SRE (Neha Kapoor, Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes) for reliability standards, runbooks, and on-call readiness; Security Engineering (Marcus Lin, Kevin Osei, Hanae Suzuki) for encryption, key management, and audit/retention requirements; Release Engineering (Connor O’Brien) for packaging, signing, and release gates; Solutions Engineering/Professional Services (Markus Klein, Colin O’Donnell, Fatima Noor, Bruno Silva) for customer-facing workflows and validation. Constraints: backups must be encrypted at rest (customer-managed keys where applicable), restorations must be deterministic and documented, and the process must work in constrained environments (air-gapped on-prem, limited outbound egress, restricted IAM). Deliverables include: Confluence runbooks and DR plans, reference scripts/CLI commands and Helm/Terraform hooks in GitHub, dashboards/alerts for backup job success and restore validation, and a testing plan validated via a DR game day.

Proposed timeline (hypothetical):
- Phase 0 (1–2 weeks): Requirements capture across 3–5 enterprise Private accounts; define RPO/RTO targets, supported storage backends, and threat model.
- Phase 1 (2–4 weeks): Design + ADR (backup format, encryption, key handling); draft runbooks; implement core scripts in installer repo.
- Phase 2 (3–6 weeks): Integrations (Helm charts, Terraform modules, observability pack); build restore validation tooling; staging DR rehearsals.
- Phase 3 (2–3 weeks): Game day + hardening; documentation finalization; release checklist + support enablement.

Success metrics: backup job success rate (per environment), time-to-restore for reference deployments, documented RPO/RTO attainment for supported architectures, and reduction in support escalations related to Private DR readiness.

files.description: Overview page for the Day-2 backup/restore toolkit: supported deployment types (VPC/on-prem), what gets backed up, what is explicitly out of scope, prerequisites, and ownership/contacts.
RPO/RTO target matrix by deployment archetype (single-region VPC, multi-AZ, on-prem, air-gapped) and by component (config DB, object storage, audit logs).
Step-by-step runbook for taking a consistent control-plane backup (pre-flight checks, quiesce steps, snapshot commands, encryption, verification, and where artifacts are stored).
Restore runbook covering restore prerequisites, bootstrap order, validation steps, rollback/abort criteria, and how to confirm tenant configuration and routing policies are restored correctly.
Guidance on what (if anything) is backed up for data-plane components; emphasizes stateless restoration patterns and what configuration must be captured for deterministic redeploy.
Disaster recovery plan for VPC single-region installs: restore into a clean cluster in the same region, DNS/TLS considerations, and validation checklist.
DR plan for on-prem / air-gapped customers: offline artifact handling, signed bundle expectations, and restore flow without external dependencies.
Supported backup storage backends and configuration examples (S3 + KMS, NFS, GCS where applicable), including retention policies and access control patterns.
Integration guide for Kubernetes backup tooling (e.g., Velero): what resources to include/exclude, how to handle secrets, and how to coordinate with Redwood’s own snapshots.
On-prem packaging doc defining offline bundle layout for backup/restore utilities, signature verification, checksum manifests, and version compatibility rules.
SRE-oriented runbook for periodic smoke tests: how to validate last backup integrity, run a restore in staging, and alert/paging criteria when tests fail.
Infrastructure runbook for cluster-level recovery: etcd snapshot restore procedure, caveats, and when to use it vs. application-level restoration.
ADR documenting chosen backup artifact format (manifest + encrypted tarball, etc.), key management approach, and rationale vs alternatives.
Security/compliance guidance for audit-log backup and retention in Private deployments: retention controls, export options, and evidence considerations.
Game day plan for DR rehearsal: scenario, roles, timelines, communication templates, success criteria, and follow-up actions.
Working spec draft (informal) capturing early requirements, open questions, and component inventory for backup/restore.
Spreadsheet-style survey results from enterprise prospects/customers: desired RPO/RTO, allowed storage backends, KMS/HSM constraints, and air-gap requirements.
Notes from a DR game day rehearsal: timeline of actions, what broke, MTTR estimates, and remediation tasks linked to Linear tickets.
Cost model sheet estimating backup storage growth and egress implications by deployment size; includes retention policy sensitivity analysis.
Release checklist for shipping the toolkit: CI gates, signing verification, docs completeness, and version compatibility checks.
Test plan for restore validation: test cases, expected outcomes, failure injection ideas, and required observability signals.
Slides-style dashboard mockups for backup success rate, restore drill latency, and alert thresholds for Private deployments.
Personal scratchpad from Bruno Silva listing edge cases encountered in customer environments (permissions, slow object storage, clock skew, missing CRDs).
PM ticket capturing requirements and acceptance criteria (supported environments, RPO/RTO, encryption, customer-facing docs deliverables).
Engineering ticket to add `backup create` command to the Private installer tooling, including artifact manifest and integrity verification.
Engineering ticket to add `restore apply` workflow, bootstrap ordering, and post-restore validation hooks.
